1.title: Analytics Rules, Anomalies and MITRE ATT&CK Coverage in Sentinel
1.text: Welcome to Module ten: Analytics Rules, Anomalies and my ter attack Coverage in Sentinel. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Configure and manage analytics rules in Microsoft Sentinel sim, including scheduled, near-real time (N R T), threat intelligence and machine learning. Analyze attack vector coverage by using the my ter attack matrix. Configure anomalies in Microsoft Sentinel. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Analytics rule types
1.text: Analytics rule types. Path: Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration, then Analytics, with tabs Active rules, Rule templates and Anomalies. To use a template, select it and choose Create rule.

1.title: Analytics rule types, continued
1.text: Analytics rule types. The figure shows this: The analytics rule types and what each is for.

1.title: Analytics rule types, continued
1.text: Analytics rule types. Scheduled. Runs a K Q L query on a schedule; the most flexible. Near-real-time (N R T). Runs every minute, for fast detections on a single table. Threat intelligence (T I map). Matches indicators against your logs; template names start with T I map. Microsoft security. Creates incidents from alerts of other Microsoft security products. Anomaly. Machine learning models that flag unusual behavior; no alerts, results go to the Anomalies table. Machine learning behavior analytics. Preview rules for S S H and R D P logons. Fusion. One rule, on by default, with hidden logic that correlates multistage attacks.

1.title: Analytics rule types, continued
1.text: Analytics rule types. In the Defender portal, Fusion is disabled and Microsoft security (incident creation) rules are not available, because Defender X D R already creates those incidents. Exam tip: Scheduled equals flexible. N R T equals one minute, one table. Anomaly rules produce no alerts.

1.title: Scheduled rules
1.text: Scheduled rules. The wizard has the steps General, Set rule logic, Incident settings, Automated response and Review plus create. Query interval and lookback. Each five minutes to fourteen days. Start running. Automatically, or At a specific time (preview; ten minutes to thirty days after creation). Ingestion delay. Allow for a five-minute delay. Query length. one to ten thousand characters; search and union are not allowed. Alert threshold. Per run: minimum, maximum or exact number of results. Event grouping. One alert per run (default), or one alert per event (up to one hundred fifty alerts, the last one summarizing the rest).

1.title: Scheduled rules, continued
1.text: Scheduled rules. Suppression. Stop running the rule for up to twenty-four hours after an alert. Results simulation. Test against the last fifty runs. Severity. Informational, Low, Medium, High.

1.title: Scheduled rules, continued
1.text: Scheduled rules. Entity mapping. Maps columns to entities (account, host, I P); required for the investigation graph. Custom details and alert details. Show extra fields and dynamic titles in the alert. Incident settings. Create incidents (on by default); group alerts into one incident (up to one hundred fifty alerts, five hours by default, five minutes to seven days). Exam tip: Without entity mappings, the investigation graph cannot be used and alerts cannot be correlated by entity.

1.title: NRT rules
1.text: N R T rules. Schedule. Every minute with a one-minute lookback; not configurable. Query. A single table; use project to keep results small. Event grouping. Per-event alerts are limited to thirty events (twenty-nine alerts plus a summary). Create. plus Create, then N R T query rule.

1.title: Threat intelligence and Microsoft security rules
1.text: Threat intelligence and Microsoft security rules. T I map rules match indicators (Module eight) with events, for example T I map I P entity to Azure Activity. Defaults: hourly run, one-hour lookback, alert when results greater than zero; lookback up to fourteen days. Microsoft Threat Intelligence Analytics is a rule that cannot be customized. A Microsoft security rule turns alerts from other Microsoft security products into incidents automatically. It is not available with Defender X D R incident integration.

1.title: Anomaly rules
1.text: Anomaly rules. Anomaly rules use machine learning to spot unusual behavior and store the results in the Anomalies table. Built-in rules. Cannot be edited. Tune. Duplicate the rule, run the duplicate in Flighting mode next to the original in Production mode. Compare. Review both results. Promote. Switch the duplicate to Production. Exam tip: Flighting equals test. Production equals live. Tune an anomaly by duplicating it, not by editing the built-in rule.

1.title: MITRE ATT&CK coverage
1.text: my ter attack coverage. Open Microsoft Sentinel, then Threat management, then my ter attack in the Defender portal. The page maps detections to attack tactics and techniques. Default. Active scheduled and N R T rules. Simulated coverage. Detections available but not yet configured, through the Simulated rules menu. View my ter by threat scenario. Filter by threat scenario (Defender portal). The my ter attack workbook and sock optimization coverage recommendations use the same mapping. Exam tip: Gaps in the matrix equals missing detections. Simulated shows what you could cover by enabling templates.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A sock needs an alert within about one minute whenever a break-glass account signs in. The query uses one table. Which rule type fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A near-real-time (N R T) rule that runs every minute. N R T rules run every minute on a single table.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A scheduled rule returns thirty matching events and creates thirty alerts. The sock wants one alert per run. Which setting should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Event grouping set to group all events into a single alert. Event grouping controls whether a run produces one alert or one alert per event; one alert per run is the default.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An engineer wants to tune a built-in anomaly rule without affecting production detections. What should the engineer do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Duplicate the rule and run the duplicate in Flighting mode. Built-in anomaly rules cannot be edited; run a duplicate in Flighting mode, compare, then promote it.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. After onboarding Sentinel to the Defender portal, an analyst cannot find the Microsoft security incident creation rule type. Why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Defender X D R already creates those incidents, so the rule type is not available. Microsoft security incident creation rules (and Fusion) are not available when Defender X D R integration is on.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An analyst wants to see which attack techniques could be covered by detections that exist as templates but are not yet enabled. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The my ter attack page with the Simulated rules menu. The my ter attack page can show simulated coverage from available but unconfigured detections.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A scheduled rule query ends with "search " to scan every table. What happens when the rule is saved? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The query is rejected because search is not allowed. Queries that use search or union are not allowed in scheduled rules.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How often does an N R T rule run? Answer: Every minute. Question two. What is the range for interval and lookback of a scheduled rule? Answer: five minutes to fourteen days. Question three. Which table receives anomaly results? Answer: Anomalies.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the maximum length of a scheduled rule query? Answer: ten thousand characters. Question five. Which feature makes the investigation graph work? Answer: Entity mapping. Question six. What does Flighting mode do? Answer: Runs a duplicate rule for testing next to the Production rule.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Path: Microsoft Sentinel, then Configuration, then Analytics. Types: Scheduled, N R T, T I map, Microsoft security, Anomaly, M L behavior, Fusion. Scheduled: five minutes to fourteen days; ten thousand characters; no search or union. N R T: every minute, one table, thirty events per-event grouping. Incidents: group up to one hundred fifty alerts, five hours by default. Anomalies: duplicate, Flighting, promote; results in the Anomalies table. my ter: active versus simulated coverage.
